title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting (continuing from p.717). Grothendieck works with a short exact sequence 1 → μ → M → M~ → 1. Here M = N_{1,1} is the profinite fundamental group of the moduli stack of elliptic curves; geometrically this is SL(2,Z)^, and probably the arithmetic version over Q is meant. M~ = N'_{1,1} = M_{0,3} is the fundamental group of the orbifold (U_{0,3,Q}, S_3) ≅ M_{1,1}'_Q, i.e. P^1−{0,1,∞} modulo S_3, the rigidified j-line; geometrically this is PSL(2,Z)^ ≅ SL(2,Z)^/±1. The group μ = {±1} = {1,ω} is the generic automorphism group of an elliptic curve. On the previous page he built a group G_{ρ,σ} from an abelian, Fermat-type quotient of π_{0,3}. This G_{ρ,σ} is an extension 1 → μ_G → G_{ρ,σ} → G~_{ρ,σ} → 1. He has a homomorphism M~ → G~_{ρ,σ}, which he interprets as the monodromy of the Fermat pro-covering of (U_{0,3},S_3). This page states that M, as an extension of M~ by μ, is recovered as the pullback of the extension G_{ρ,σ} → G~_{ρ,σ} along M~ → G~_{ρ,σ}. Formally this follows from the morphism of extensions (298), since its kernel map μ_M → μ_G is an isomorphism. He then notes a 'striking analogy' with §48. There he started instead from the 'Lie-type' quotient SL(2,Ẑ) of π_{0,3}^{+∧}. That gave a homomorphism M_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}, essentially the Tate-module, Galois-enriched representation of the universal elliptic curve. The same central extension M = N_{1,1} was then recovered as the pullback of GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}. His programme is to make anabelian-geometric facts explicit as automorphisms of profinite objects (likely groupoids or torsors) based at π_{0,3}^. The 'remarkable fact' is that two quite different quotients both recover the same central extension: an abelian/Fermat quotient and an SL_2/Lie-type quotient. The next page explains this. In both cases the quotient he started from was a quotient of SL(2,Z)^ ≅ N_{1,1} itself, not of PSL(2,Z)^. The next page also leaves open a 'fibre type' interpretation of G_{ρ,σ}, analogous to the 'Fermat torus'.
errors: No mathematical error. The pullback reconstruction is formal: any morphism of extensions that is an isomorphism on kernels identifies the source extension with the pullback. The 'remarkable' coincidence therefore reduces to the existence of the lift M → G (or M → GL(2,Ẑ)) that is injective on μ, which the next page itself acknowledges.
Notation is inconsistent across pages (μ = {1,ω} vs {±1}; π_{0,3}^{+∧} vs π_{0,3}^∧), but this is harmless.

ideas.what: Recovering the central ±1 extension (stack M_{1,1} over its rigidification, the j-line orbifold (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3) as a pullback of the extension GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 via the Tate-module representation.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy representation π_1(M_{1,1}) → GL_2(Ẑ); rigidification of the generic μ_2 inertia (Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli style rigidification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Tate module, modular group); stack rigidification by Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli (2003)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z)^ but not this exact pullback statement

ideas.what: Recovering the same extension via an abelian/Fermat quotient of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) (the Fermat pro-covering and a group G_{ρ,σ} of its automorphisms, with S_3 symmetry).
ideas.modern_name: Galois/monodromy action on the Fermat tower (metabelian quotient); Ihara's universal power series for Jacobi sums, Anderson's hyperadelic gamma function

ideas.what: Programme of expressing anabelian-geometric data as automorphisms of profinite objects (groupoids/torsors) based at π_{0,3}^, including Galois-enriched versions.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), La Longue Marche (1981)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly juxtaposes two routes to the same central extension SL(2,Z)^ of PSL(2,Z)^ (with arithmetic enrichment). One is abelian (the Fermat pro-covering, with symmetry group G_{ρ,σ}); the other is Lie-type (SL_2, Tate modules). He treats their agreement as a phenomenon calling for a general explanation. Comparing the Ihara/Anderson Fermat-Jacobian picture with the elliptic GL_2 picture at the level of this μ_2 extension is not a standard explicit theme.
missed.quote: Il y a une analogie frappante avec ce qui s'était passé, d'ailleurs, quand on était parti (cf. § 48 ...) des quotients ("du type Lie") Sl(2,Ẑ)' de π_{0,3}^{+∧}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It suggests treating the abelian (Fermat/Jacobi-sum) and modular (GL_2) quotients of π_1(M_{1,1}) uniformly as 'S_3-equivariant quotients lifting to SL(2,Z)^'. That viewpoint is relevant to equivariant Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, but the content is largely formal.

missed.claim: He seeks a geometric 'fibre type' interpretation (like the 'Fermat torus') of the full group G_{ρ,σ}, not only of G~_{ρ,σ}, as automorphisms of a not-too-large fibre object. He leaves this open on the next page.
missed.quote: Si on cherche malgré tout une interprétation (genre "tore de Fermat") de l'hom M → G_{p,σ} ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would amount to a modular, stack-level interpretation of the Fermat tower over M_{1,1}, related to the Legendre/Fermat-quartic links between elliptic curves and Fermat curves. It is a small open thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reflective remark on an analogy whose content is a formal pullback-of-extensions argument; the substantive constructions are on neighbouring pages. The stated Fermat-vs-Lie-type parallel is mildly interesting but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'G_{\varphi,\sigma}' should be G_{\rho,\sigma} (consistent with the previous page); the manuscript letter is a ρ-like stroke.
'des quotients quotient ("du type Lie")' — the duplicated 'quotient' is a transcription artifact; read 'des quotients ("du type Lie")'.
'Sl(2,\hat{\mathbb Z}^{?})'' — the manuscript reads roughly Sl(2,Ẑ^{4})' or Sl(2,Ẑ)' with a superscript mark; the superscript is uncertain.
'π_{0,3}^{+∧}' is written with a crossed-out/circled capital (likely Π or 𝔖) and superscript '+∧'.
'[-Mor-]' before M_{0,3} is a crossed-out word (likely the start of 'Mor' or 'M_0'); likewise a crossed-out letter before "l'ext.".
'Du pt de vue actuel ici j'essaye' — possibly 'Du pt de vue actuel, où j'essaye'.
'de 𝒢-vs [?] {+profini+} à base' — possibly 'de groupoïdes profinis à base Π_{0,3}^∧' or '𝔊-torseurs'; uncertain.
